nodes.title: Round 7's pre-registered rule (harness/rule.txt): gpt-4.1-mini single MATCHES tiered on the shipped outcome-first contract. Exact McNemar mini vs tiered: 0 discordant on outcome, objections, every moment and commitments, same pass and crossed (p = 1.0), pooled 0 of 84 pairs; 0/42 any-field disagreement on each same-pass pair. nodes.title: On the outcome-first contract tiered's escalation path has not fired on the bench (0/117 analysed TEST calls over rounds 6-7; every recorded outcome at confidence >= 0.9, threshold 0.6): what does tiered add over gpt-4.1-mini single on calls where the first pass is unsure or finds no outcome, and how often are such calls on real traffic?
nodes.closes_when: A slice on which the first pass actually escalates (consented real-traffic calls, or a synthetic hard-case set pre-registered before its first request: ambiguous or hedged outcomes, mixed language, long calls) runs gpt-4.1-mini single against tiered, two passes each. Tiered better by 2 or more calls per 42 or with exact McNemar p < 0.05 reopens the analysis default; otherwise mini single stands. The escalation rate on real traffic is logged with n.

nodes.title: Per-call analysis defaults to gpt-4.1-mini single on the shipped outcome-first contract; tiered (mini first, gpt-4.1 at threshold 0.6) and gpt-4.1 stay selectable. Adopted by the integrator under round 7's pre-registered rule; the code default (defaultAnalysisSetting) moves with it, and the product counts the calls tiered would have escalated (first-pass confidence under 0.6) so real traffic can answer the open escalation question
nodes.rationale: decision.2026-10-24.analysis-default-tiered's reverse_if is met: on the shipped contract, mini single matched tiered on TEST in two consecutive rounds (round 6: 42, 42 vs 42; round 7: 42, 42 vs 42, 42) with no outcome, objection, moment, commitment or crisis loss and 0 discordant pairs on any field. Round 7's rule, written before its first request, recommends the cheaper option on a match. What bounds this: tiered escalated 0/117 analysed calls over rounds 6-7, so on the bench its requests were mini's, and it cost the same (Rs 0.0514-0.0521 per model-analysed call against mini's 0.0515-0.0519). The saving, and any quality tiered adds, exist only on calls where the first pass is unsure or finds no outcome, which this bench no longer contains (open.2026-10-24.analysis-escalation-path-unexercised). On earlier contracts tiered did catch mini's false nulls (rounds 3-5: 250/252 vs 234/252); outcome-first removed them on this bench (complaint and wrong-person 24/24 (pass, call) pairs over rounds 6-7). Adopted rather than held: the reverse_if was written before rounds 6-7 and is met by its letter; keeping tiered on an unmeasured benefit is the post-hoc override pre-registration exists to prevent. The risk this leaves (unsure calls on real traffic get mini's answer, not gpt-4.1's) is bounded by counting would-escalate calls in the product, which is the slice the open question needs.
nodes.reverse_if: On the shipped contract, a TEST round in which mini single is more than 1 call below tiered on either pass, or loses an objection, moment or commitment against it; or a slice on which tiered actually escalates (real traffic or a pre-registered hard-case set) where tiered beats mini single by 2 or more calls per 42 or with exact McNemar p < 0.05; or a contract change that brings back mini's complaint or wrong-person false nulls.
